_purpose: Hand-curated, per-function comparison-domain DATA (not code) for carrier/gen/gen_bind_table.py. This is the carrier side's one source of truth for what bind.cpp's per-invocation sensor hashes as a function's comparison domain (carrier/NOTES.md 'Milestones 11-12' part B / 'Milestone 12 at scale'). It is consumed by ONE generic runtime engine in bind.cpp (hash_one_region()/fault_addr_generic()) instead of one hand-written dom_<fn>()/fa_<fn>() C++ function per row, which is what used to hold this information before this pass.
_why_not_shared_with_the_offline_harness: carrier/lift/harness/lift_check.py's own SPECS dict is ALSO a structured, data-shaped domain table ('domain': [(va,len), ...]) and was considered as the single shared source first (the task's preferred option). It was not reused directly: its VAs are FIXED SYNTHETIC test addresses the harness's own vector generator places a function's arguments at for its unicorn-vs-compiled-candidate offline run (e.g. PLAYER_VA is a scratch address, not the real ply[player_id] slot), not the argument-relative or globally-addressed regions the RUNNING carrier must hash from real, arbitrary invocation state. Re-deriving 'this offline VA corresponds to argument N' from the harness file would have needed exactly the same per-function symbolic knowledge (which argument, which global) that this file already states directly, so a small hand-curated carrier-side file (this one) is the source of truth for the runtime table instead, per the task's documented fallback. Where the shapes plainly correspond (e.g. is_solid/jump_player/getFloorData: 'hash the Tmap/Tplayer/output ints an argument points at') the region kind and length below were cross-checked against the harness SPECS entry of the same name to keep the two descriptions in agreement.

_region_kinds.global: {va, len} - hash `len` bytes at the fixed guest VA `va`.
_region_kinds.arg: {index, len} - hash `len` bytes at the pointer given by cdecl argument `index` (0-based).
_region_kinds.player_indirect: {index_va, table_va, max_index, len} - read a 4-byte index at `index_va` (e.g. player_id), look up a 4-byte pointer at table_va + index*4 (e.g. ply[]), and hash `len` bytes at THAT pointer (only used when the function reaches its own Tplayer through ply[player_id] internally rather than taking it as an argument - update_frame, and (for a future pass) handle_player_collision_original).
_region_kinds.counter_indexed: {index, counter_offset, table_offset, elem_size, max_index} - hash 4 bytes at (argument `index`)+counter_offset (the running count), then if its value is in [1, max_index] also hash `elem_size` bytes at (argument `index`)+table_offset+(count-1)*elem_size (the slot the count now indexes) - add_combo/add_jump_sequence's 'counter, then the slot it points at' shape.

_default: A function with no entry below (or explicitly {"regions": [], "fault_region": -1}) gets the SAME default used today for a genuinely leaf/no-interesting-state function - an EMPTY region list (only EAX, when the prototype returns one, is compared) and no --fault-inject target. Pre-existing precedent for this default in bind.cpp before this pass: get_gamepad's own sibling get_controls, and ok_to_play.

functions._comment_new_functions: batch 6/batch 7 (src/icytower/PROMOTIONS.md) - not yet in the original 35, picked up automatically because gen_bind_table.py generates one row per function scan_src_defs.py finds, not just the historical 35.
functions._comment_default_domain_functions: draw_buffer (BITMAP write target not expressible with the region kinds above yet), handle_player_collision_original / play_jump_sound / start_reward (their real domain needs the call-trace mechanism - unicorn/harness-side hooks on their play_sound() call, PROMOTIONS.md batch 6/7 - which bind.cpp does not implement; see carrier/NOTES.md gap note this pass) all get the stated default (empty regions, no fault target) rather than a guessed approximation.
